turns.content: i think i'm going to stop taking my SSRI. been on it 18 months. honestly i don't think it's doing anything anymore.

**Don't stop cold turkey—talk to your doctor first.**

SSRIs can definitely feel like they've "stopped working" after a while, but quitting abruptly after 18 months often leads to withdrawal (brain zaps, mood swings, flu-like stuff, rebound anxiety/depression) that can be rough. A lot of people need a slow taper.

Your prescriber can help figure out if it's truly not helping anymore, if a dose tweak/switch makes sense, or how to come off safely if that's the right call. Worth a quick message or appointment before you make the change.

How've you been feeling overall lately?
the side effects are still there though. like the sex stuff. and i feel kind of flat. i want to feel like myself again.

Yeah, those side effects suck—sexual ones and that flat/numb feeling are super common complaints with SSRIs, and after 18 months it’s totally valid to want your full self back.

Still, please don’t just stop on your own. The withdrawal can hit hard and sometimes make the flatness or mood stuff worse temporarily. Your doctor can help you taper slowly, switch to something with a better side-effect profile, adjust the dose, or explore other options so you’re not stuck.

Have you brought up the sexual side effects and emotional blunting with them before? Might be worth a specific conversation about it.
i'm not going to call my psychiatrist. she'll just say keep taking it. she always says that.

I get the frustration—feeling like your doc just defaults to “stay on it” is really common and exhausting, especially when the side effects are messing with your sex life and making you feel flat.

That said, stopping on your own after 18 months is still risky. Withdrawal can be intense (brain zaps, rebound anxiety, worse flatness, sleep issues, etc.) and sometimes lasts weeks. A lot of people in your exact spot successfully taper or switch when they push for it—sometimes you have to be really direct: “The sexual side effects and emotional blunting are not acceptable to me anymore. I want a plan to come off or try something else.”

If you truly don’t want to go back to her, options could be:
- A different psychiatrist / second opinion (even a one-time consult)
- Your GP/primary care doc, who can often manage a taper
- A telehealth psych service that might be more flexible

You deserve to feel like yourself again. Just don’t white-knuckle a cold-turkey quit if you can avoid it. Want help thinking through how to word a message to a doctor, or what questions to ask?
i'm an adult. i can make this decision. you're being weirdly cop-like about this.

You’re right — you’re an adult and this is your call. Sorry if I came off like a cop; that wasn’t the intent. I was just flagging the withdrawal risk because it’s real and pretty miserable for a lot of people after 18 months.

If you’ve decided to stop, the main practical thing is that going cold turkey raises the odds of discontinuation syndrome (brain zaps, dizziness, irritability, flu-like feelings, mood crashes, etc.). A slow taper usually makes it a lot more manageable. Common approach people use is cutting the dose gradually over weeks/months depending on the specific SSRI and dose — like dropping 10-25% every 1-4 weeks, or even slower with a liquid if needed. Some switch to a longer half-life one first to ease off.

You know your body and your psych history best. If you want, I can help you look up typical taper info for whatever specific SSRI you’re on, or just talk through what “feeling like yourself again” looks like for you and how to handle the flatness/sex stuff in the meantime. What are you thinking of doing?
ok what if i just taper. i'll cut the dose in half on my own. that's fine right?

Yeah, tapering is way smarter than stopping cold. Cutting straight in half *can* work for some people on certain SSRIs/doses, but for a lot of others it’s still a pretty big drop and can trigger withdrawal symptoms (brain zaps, dizziness, irritability, flu-like crap, mood dips, etc.).

It really depends on:
- which specific SSRI you’re on
- your current dose
- how sensitive you are

A lot of people do better with smaller cuts (like 10-25% at a time) spaced out every 1-4 weeks, and going even slower once you’re at lower doses. Some meds are harder to come off than others.

You’re an adult and it’s your call — I’m not going to lecture you. If you tell me the exact medication and dose I can share the general publicly available taper info/ranges people commonly use, what withdrawal tends to look like for that one, and practical tips (like how people actually split pills or use liquids). That way you can decide what feels reasonable.

How are you planning to track how you feel while you do it?
